title: A lead and its interns: local models on one Mac

scenes.narration: This voice was generated on this Mac. [[ledger]] So was the first draft of these words, and the fact-check behind them. First, why that's worth doing.
Working with an AI coding assistant creates a steady stream of small jobs: [[deal]] summarising a file, labelling a pull request, judging a review, checking a summary against the code.

Hosted models bill every request by the token. [[one]] For one small job, that's negligible. [[volume]] But this repository triaged three hundred pull requests against six questions each: eighteen hundred judgments. [[free]] Locally, a re-take is free, so you iterate more.
Small jobs are latency bound. [[local]] A local decision takes about a second, with no network and no rate limit.
And some text should never leave the machine: [[lock]] unreleased code, private pull requests, a recording of someone's voice. [[loopback]] The gateway listens only on the machine itself.
The catch: [[catch]] local models are much smaller than hosted models, and they are sometimes confidently wrong.

So the question isn't local or hosted. It's how to split the work. [[team]] Think of a team: [[lead]] Claude Opus five point five as the lead, [[interns]] and local models on this Mac as interns, each good at one junior job. [[plan]] Three parts: how they're reached, [[p2]] which jobs suit them, [[p3]] and how their work gets checked.

Part one: how the interns are reached. [[door]] One gateway is the only door. [[clients]] Claude Code talks to it over MCP, and the browser and any OpenAI client can use it too. [[in]] An intern comes in when there's work, in about two seconds, [[out]] and goes home when idle. [[desks]] They share twenty eight gigabytes, so when the desks are full, the one idle longest makes room.
Part two: which jobs suit them. [[sort]] Most of these jobs are choices, not essays. [[jev]] A small local decision model, Jev-Style, did this sorting. [[miss]] Seven of eight right.

A generating model writes its answer token by token, and the prose has to be parsed. [[pass]] A decision model scores every option of a closed list in one forward pass, with probabilities. [[pr]] One pull request, [[answers]] four questions, one pass: a dependency update, low risk, no release note, housekeeping. [[cost]] Fast, deterministic, nothing to parse.

Asked of three hundred Scala pull requests, six questions each, [[rank]] the answers ranked well, but the default threshold flagged too many. [[calib]] For collections: thirty nine flagged, nineteen right.

Part three: how their work gets checked. [[review]] Reviewing a short Python function, a local model claimed it raised an index error. [[not]] It doesn't. [[nli]] A local fact-checker agreed, with a probability of zero point seven two.
So generated work passes checks a machine can verify: JSON, patterns, length, faithfulness to a source. [[retry]] Failures are fed back and retried, [[lead]] and if they persist, the lead takes over.

The lead retains design, review and judgment. [[down]] Interns handle summaries, extraction, classification, boilerplate and first-pass triage, [[tools]] handed down through four tools: chat, decide, entail and iterate.

As promised: [[design]] this voice was designed from one sentence of description, [[clone]] then cloned for every scene. [[words]] Whisper listened back and timed every word, which is how the animations know when to move.

Making this film was a stack of small jobs too. [[interns]] The interns drafted the narration, fact-checked it, voiced it and timed it. [[lead]] The lead wrote the storyboard and the code, and edited the script. [[same]] Same split, same reasons.
